title: Completed integral point tensor and scalar squares
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D and prime l!=p. There exist integral point tensor data I(E) for every finite E/Q_l [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-system] and canonical model witnesses C(E) [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-models]. Thus their completion maps have the specified quotient tensor first coordinate, zero shifted Roos coordinate, derived inverse tensor comparison and constant-section unit. For every finite coefficient embedding E->L, these same witnesses obey the actual scalarTensorChain square [def-sf-point-integral-scalar-square]. No rational, algebraically closed, or finite quotient family is asserted.

proof.text: At the integral stage put $C=\Gamma_sM$, $D=\Gamma_sN$. Their cohomology is bounded and finitely generated by [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness](2), so they admit bounded finite-projective models by [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius](2). The completed tensor is constructible and reduces to $M_j\otimes^L_{A_{E,j}}N_j$ by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible](2), where $M_j,N_j$ are the derived reductions.

source.place: Coefficient finiteness of lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness (2) and the DVR perfectness clause of lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius (2); integral reduction formula of lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible (2). Agent-written, old item step 4 (models) and step 5 (reductions).

proof.text: Sections is exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] and preserves countable products, which are exact and sectionwise by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Countable products of ordinary $\mathcal O_E$-modules are exact, since a tuple lifts coordinatewise along surjections; so both categories satisfy the hypotheses of the next lemma. Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] to sections and the strict tensor tower; its specified comparison preserves both Roos coordinates and coaugmentations. The ambient tensor comparison [lem-sf-point-ringed-evaluation-model] and the natural reduction comparison [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction] identify its levels with $(C\otimes^L_RA_j)\otimes^L_{A_j}(D\otimes^L_RA_j)$. The quotient-coordinate formulas of [lem-sf-perfect-tensor-roos-completion] identify this tower with the reductions of $C\otimes^L_RD$ and make its coaugmentation invertible. Compose the evaluated-limit identification with its inverse. This is the integral comparison; the first coordinate is the quotient tensor map and the shifted coordinate is zero. Naturality, units, signed constraints and reduction squares follow from the cited Roos and tensor model lemmas. For scalar extension use the source tensor comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] and the normalized fibre comparison of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]; their squares are the balanced scalar/completion squares of those model lemmas, including identity and iterated extensions.

lean.statement:
theorem pointIntegralCompletedTensorComparisons
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p) :
    ∃ I : ∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
      [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E], PointIntegralTensorData D l hl E,
      ∃ C : ∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
        [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E], PointIntegralTensorCanonical D l hl E (I E),
        ∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
          [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra ℚ_[l] L]
          [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] L] (ι : E →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] L),
          PointIntegralTensorScalarSquare D l hl E L ι (I E) (I L) (C E) (C L)
